title: Make Ten Card Game
subject: math
learningGoal: Find pairs of numbers that make 10, a key building block for adding.
realWorldHook: Making 10 is a shortcut grown-ups use to add in their heads.

materials.item: A deck of cards with picture cards removed

noPurchaseRoute: Write numbers 1 to 9 twice on small paper squares.
parentPreview: A quick card game: turn over cards and find pairs that add to 10. It builds fast recall of number bonds to 10.

parent.parentSays: I'm thinking of two numbers that add to 10. Can you guess one pair?

child.screen: Two numbers that make 10. Can you think of one?
child.readAloudText: Can you think of two numbers that make ten?

parent.parentSays: Lay out 8 cards face up. Take turns finding two that make 10. Say the sum out loud.
parent.whyThisWorks: Saying '7 and 3 make 10' links the pair to the total.

child.readAloudText: Find two cards that make ten.

parent.parentSays: If I have a 6, what card do I need?

child.screen: You have 6. What do you need to make 10?
child.readAloudText: You have six. What do you need to make ten?

parent.parentSays: How did you work out the partner? Fingers? Counting up?

child.screen: How did you find the partner number?
child.readAloudText: How did you find the partner number? Tell your grown-up.

parent.parentSays: Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
Which pairs are easiest? Which are tricky?

misconceptions.signal: Counts every dot on both cards from 1 each time.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Can you start from the bigger number and count on?

misconceptions.signal: Gets close but one away (e.g. 6 and 5).
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Let's check on fingers: show 6, how many fingers are down?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: You have 7 stickers and need 10 for a page. How many more?

interpretation.clear: Says 3 and links it to the game.

child.screen: You have 7 stickers. You need 10. How many more?
child.readAloudText: You have seven stickers. You need ten. How many more?

shorterVersion.description: Skip the game; do the missing number and checks.

accessibilityAdaptations: Use cards with dots so your child can count.
Use ten fingers as a visual.
